content.comment_body: Hello programmers! Interesting question about [product_name]. I have a smart home system using [product_name], and I record both outside and inside temperatures using the Data Log block. My question is: how can I read this data directly in Excel? At the moment, I use [product_name] engineering software by going online and uploading the data log. What I see in the picture is attached. Thank you for your comments. If anyone is interested in the system, I can upload my program.

With the [product_name] [article_no], you can create a data log file and save it as a CSV file onto a Micro SD card. This file can then be accessed either through [product_name] engineering software or by using the SD card directly on a PC, then imported into Excel. Refer to the manual, chapter 7, Data Log. [document]

From the manual: "You can only upload the most recent data log file on the micro SD card from [product_name] to [product_name] engineering software." That's what I currently do. My question is: How can I download the log directly with Excel? I know it's a CSV file, and I do this process regularly, but I prefer not to always open the engineering software, connect online, download the log, open the CSV, and reformat the file. Ideally, I'd just open Excel, get external data, format it, and have my file ready.

Hello [user_name], Have you figured out whether your question is possible? I'm interested in the same shortcut, so I don't have to give all my customers the [product_name] engineering software package, which is risky because it could allow changes to the PLC program. Regards,

Hello [user_name], There's a free software that converts archive formats, including .csv to .xls. I just tested it with a data log file and it worked perfectly. [url] I think this could help. Maybe we can automate Excel to do this like you imagined—Excel is quite powerful. I'll study this further. Take care.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are looking for a faster and simpler way to access data logs from [product_name] systems without relying on the engineering software every time. The current process is seen as cumbersome due to multiple steps for extracting, converting, and formatting the data for Excel. Community members want a more direct workflow or shortcut to import data into Excel with minimal effort and less risk of altering device configurations.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to import data logs directly from [product_name] into Excel, without repeated use of the engineering software, and with fewer steps. They want the process to be efficient and user-friendly, preferably allowing full integration with Excel.
